justification_text:
At the time of the forecast, the price appeared to be trading near the 324–325 level, so the one-day point estimate of 324.5 reflects very little expected movement over such a short horizon. For a single trading session, mean reversion and intraday momentum tend to dominate, and absent a known catalyst, the most defensible estimate is simply close to the last observed price. The one-week estimate of 326 incorporates a slight upward drift assumption consistent with the modest positive bias that equities and many risk assets have shown over short horizons in trending markets. The one-month estimate of 330 extends that drift further, assuming continued gradual appreciation without a major shock, while acknowledging that over four weeks there is considerably more room for the underlying trend to assert itself or reverse.

The confidence interval widths reflect how uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, a range of 312 to 337 — roughly plus or minus 4% — captures typical daily volatility including the possibility of a gap open on surprise news. By one week, the interval widens to 303–349, reflecting that intraweek volatility accumulates and a single bad session or macro release can shift the trajectory meaningfully. The one-month interval of 285–375 is deliberately wide because a full calendar month introduces exposure to earnings announcements, central bank decisions, geopolitical developments, and shifts in market sentiment that are essentially unpredictable in their timing and magnitude.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals on the downside include a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as an unexpected spike in unemployment or a negative inflation surprise prompting an aggressive policy response — or a geopolitical shock that triggers a broad risk-off move. A credit event or liquidity crisis in a systemically important institution could also produce moves well beyond the stated ranges within days. On the upside, a surprisingly dovish central bank pivot, a strong earnings season beat, or a resolution of an ongoing geopolitical tension could drive prices significantly above 375 over a month.

It is worth noting that these intervals, while wide, are not guarantees of containing all outcomes. A true tail event — the kind of move seen in March 2020 or during the 2008 financial crisis — could easily breach even the one-month interval. The 90% confidence framing means roughly one in ten outcomes is expected to fall outside the range, and in financial markets, those tail outcomes tend to be more extreme than a normal distribution would suggest, given the well-documented fat-tailed nature of returns.
